BMEN 101.description: Introduction to topics comprising the field of Biomedical Engineering, including their ethical impacts. Familiarization with resources and basic skills necessary to succeed in this major and field.
BMEN 101.subject: BMEN
BMEN 101.title: Introduction to Biomedical Engineering

BMEN 212.description: Fundamentals of static equilibrium, free body diagrams, force and momentum balances; introduction to linear circuit analysis.
BMEN 212.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 115 or higher or placement through the Math Assessment of Prerequisites (MAP).
BMEN 212.subject: BMEN
BMEN 212.title: Fundamentals of Biomedical Systems

BMEN 240.description: Introduction to molecular, cellular, and physical biology principles and concepts and application of engineering principles to further the understanding of biological systems. Protein and nucleic acid structure and function; DNA replication, mutations, and repair; transcription, translation, and post-translational processing; cellular organization; molecular transport and trafficking; and cellular models.
BMEN 240.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 101.
BMEN 240.subject: BMEN
BMEN 240.title: Cellular and Molecular Biology with Engineering Applications

BMEN 263.description: Mathematical and theoretical analysis of the mechanical properties and functions of materials, including those of biological origin and clinical relevance. Stress, strain, mechanical properties of materials, axial loading, torsion, bending, and stress/strain transformations. Application of the categories and methodology of solid and fluid mechanics to study biological tissues and events.
BMEN 263.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BMEN 212 and PHYS 211.
BMEN 263.subject: BMEN
BMEN 263.title: Introduction to Biomechanics

BMEN 270.description: Molecular properties of biomaterials including natural, polymeric, ceramic, metallic, and composite biomaterials; mechanical properties, surface modification, degradation, protein adsorption, blood, cell and tissue interaction of biomaterials; host response to implanted biomaterials; rational design of biomaterials.
BMEN 270.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 101.
BMEN 270.subject: BMEN
BMEN 270.title: Materials in Medicine

BMEN 271.description: Properties of metals, ceramics, polymers, natural materials and composites; methods to modify surface and bulk properties of biomaterials; mechanisms of degradation in physiological environments; cell- and tissue-biomaterial interactions; host response to implanted biomaterials; blood-biomaterial interactions; rational design of biomaterials for specific biomedical applications.
BMEN 271.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in CHEM 333; C or better in BMEN 290 or ECHE 311.
BMEN 271.subject: BMEN
BMEN 271.title: Introduction to Biomaterials

BMEN 290.description: First, second, and third law of thermodynamics; free energy and chemical equilibrium in biological processes; phase equilibrium for biomedical systems; energy and metabolism; membrane potentials and depolarization.
BMEN 290.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BMEN 240 and PHYS 211.
BMEN 290.subject: BMEN
BMEN 290.title: Thermodynamics of Biomolecular Systems

BMEN 302.description: Analysis and discussion of biomedical industries, standards, regulations, products, and patents. Ethical issues associated with research, introduction of new products, animal subjects, and human subjects.
BMEN 302.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 101 or ENCP 101.
BMEN 302.subject: BMEN
BMEN 302.title: Professional Development and Ethics in Biomedical Engineering

BMEN 303.description: Analysis and discussion of industries, products, patents, industrial inventiveness, and biomedical research. Ethical issues associated with research, introduction of new products, animal subjects, and human subjects.
BMEN 303.subject: BMEN
BMEN 303.title: Professional Development and Ethics in Biomedical Engineering

BMEN 321.description: Basic electric circuits and equivalent cell model circuits used in biomonitoring and electrophysiology. Ohm’s and Kirchoff’s Laws. Applications of electrical components, such as operations amplifiers, filter, and Wheastone bridge, in biomonitoring and electrophysiology. Origins of bioelectricity. Biopotential and electrochemistry including Nernst and Goldman-Hudgkin-Katz equations for describing membrane potential of nerve and muscle cells. Ion transport involved in maintaining cell pH, action potential, muscle contraction, sensory perception.
BMEN 321.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BMEN 212, C or better in BMEN 240, C or better in MATH 242.
BMEN 321.subject: BMEN
BMEN 321.title: Biomonitoring and Electrophysiology

BMEN 340.description: Introduction to principles of organic chemistry and biochemistry as applied to biomedical engineering. Molecular, cellular, and physical biology principles and concepts with application of engineering principles. Introduction to biomanufacturing, bioinformatics, and advanced mathematical cellular models.
BMEN 340.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BMEN 240.
BMEN 340.subject: BMEN
BMEN 340.title: Biochemistry with Engineering Applications

BMEN 342.description: Qualitative and quantitative aspects of infectious diseases; principles of diagnosis and control. Elements of human immunological response and immune disorders; influence on biomedical engineering of explants and implants.
BMEN 342.subject: BMEN
BMEN 342.title: Infectious Disease Immunology for Biomedical Engineers

BMEN 345.description: Foundations for biomedical engineering with a focus on human anatomy and physiology. Introduction to the inter-relationships between tissue/organ structure and function; demonstration of how an engineering approach can promote understanding of these relationships. Recent biomedical engineering advances and their relations to underlying anatomy and physiology.
BMEN 345.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BMEN 240.
BMEN 345.subject: BMEN
BMEN 345.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology for Biomedical Engineers

BMEN 346.description: Qualitative and quantitative aspects of human system based medical microbiology; principles of diagnosis and control of representative human diseases. Elements of human immunological response and immune disorders.
BMEN 346.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 101.
BMEN 346.subject: BMEN
BMEN 346.title: Medical Microbiology for Biomedical Engineers

BMEN 354.description: Basics of convective and diffusive transport applied to biological and biomedical systems. The effect of fluid flow and mass transport upon biochemical interactions. Scaling and design of biotransport systems.
BMEN 354.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 263 and C or better in MATH 242.
BMEN 354.subject: BMEN
BMEN 354.title: Biotransport

BMEN 360.description: Introduction to analytical methods as used in biomedicine. Applications of bioinstrumentation in disease diagnosis.
BMEN 360.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 345 and BMEN 240.
BMEN 360.subject: BMEN
BMEN 360.title: Biomedical Analysis

BMEN 363.description: Sensing and measurement of biophysical and biochemical properties and signals in the human body for quantitative molecular, cell, and tissue analysis. Overview on the theory, design and application of common biomedical instrumentation used for diagnosis, treatment, and scientific study of physiological parameters in clinical medicine and biomedical research.
BMEN 363.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 321 or BMEN 360.
BMEN 363.subject: BMEN
BMEN 363.title: Biomedical Instrumentation

BMEN 381.description: Introduction to laboratory techniques and tools used for physiological measurements in biomedical engineering, with focus on biological, physical, and biomaterial methods. Data processing and analysis, as well as effective communication of results in written and oral form.
BMEN 381.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 263, D or better in STAT 509.
BMEN 381.subject: BMEN
BMEN 381.title: Biomedical Engineering Laboratory I

BMEN 382.description: Introduction to laboratory techniques and tools used for physiological measurements in biomedical engineering, with focus on measurement of biosignals and common analytical methods employed in biomedical research and clinical settings. Data processing and analysis, as well as effective communication of results in written and oral form.
BMEN 382.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 321 and BMEN 381.
BMEN 382.subject: BMEN
BMEN 382.title: Biomedical Engineering Laboratory II

BMEN 389.description: Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title. May be repeated as topic varies.
BMEN 389.subject: BMEN
BMEN 389.title: Special Topics in Biomedical Engineering for Undergraduates

BMEN 391.description: Kinetic theory applied to biomedical systems, including enzymatic reactions, cell growth, and kinetic models of biological systems.
BMEN 391.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 340, CHEM 550, or BIOL 541; C or better in BMEN 290, ECHE 310, EMCH 290, or ENCP 290; C or better in MATH 242.
BMEN 391.subject: BMEN
BMEN 391.title: Kinetics in Biomolecular Systems

BMEN 392.description: Biological systems are used in chemical industries for a wide variety of applications, including the formation of important products (e.g. pharmaceuticals), sensor technology, degradation, and waste water treatment. This class will provide an overview of materials needed to investigate and model biosystems.
BMEN 392.subject: BMEN
BMEN 392.title: Fundamentals of Biochemical Engineering

BMEN 411.description: Introduction to modern computational modeling tools used in biomedical engineering. Analysis, visualization and image processing using engineering software as applied to problems of interest in biomedical engineering.
BMEN 411.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 271 and BMEN 354.
BMEN 411.subject: BMEN
BMEN 411.title: Modeling and Simulation of Biomedical Systems

BMEN 427.description: Integrated team work/project management, voice of the patient , design specifications, design functions, design concepts, economic factors, concept selection and product architecture. The initial feasibility study, selection of the final design approach, and preliminary specifications are required by the end of the semester.
BMEN 427.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 381 or BMEN 382.
BMEN 427.subject: BMEN
BMEN 427.title: Senior Biomedical Engineering Design I

BMEN 428.description: Design for manufacturability, ergonomic and aesthetic considerations, prototype construction and testing, fabrication and biological testing of tissue engineered constructs, statistical methods/design of experiments, ethics/product liability and social/environmental impact. The final engineering design (specifications, drawings, bill of materials, including assessment of economics) will be completed by the end of the semester. Both written and oral reports are to be provided.
BMEN 428.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 427.
BMEN 428.subject: BMEN
BMEN 428.title: Senior Biomedical Engineering Design II

BMEN 499.description: Individual investigation or studies of special topics. A maximum of 3 credits may be applied to Biomedical Engineering program requirements. Contract approval by instructor, department, and college is required.
BMEN 499.subject: BMEN
BMEN 499.title: Independent Research

BMEN 532.description: Basic fluid mechanics, capillary, drop and micro/nanoparticle, electrokinetics; micropump, mixer, preconcentrator, electrophoresis, microactuator and particle manipulator; sensors for pressure, velocity, concentration, temperature in environmental monitoring/biodefence, clinical diagnostics, drug discovery/delivery.
BMEN 532.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in CHEM 112 and CHEM112L or CHEM 142.
BMEN 532.subject: BMEN
BMEN 532.title: Micro/nanofluidics and Lab-on-a-Chip

BMEN 537.description: Fundamentals of nano- and microfabrication, metrology and their applications in biomedical engineering and science. The fabrication covers photolithography, nano/microfabrication for nano/microstructures, etching and additive techniques, MEMS integration and packaging, etc. Metrology focuses on characterization of nanostructures with imaging technologies.
BMEN 537.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in CHEM 112 and CHEM 112L or CHEM 142.
BMEN 537.subject: BMEN
BMEN 537.title: Bio Nano/Micro Electro-Mechanical Systems

BMEN 546.description: Routes of administration; mechanisms of drug absorption and biological barriers; pharmacokinetic modeling of drug distribution; drug excretion and biotransformation; design and evaluation of controlled release systems, targeted release systems, and responsive release systems.
BMEN 546.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 345.
BMEN 546.subject: BMEN
BMEN 546.title: Delivery of Bioactive Agents

BMEN 547.description: Engineering approaches to study and control immune reactions and their applications in therapy and diagnostics for infectious disease, cancer, allergy, autoimmunity, and transplantation.
BMEN 547.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BMEN 240.
BMEN 547.subject: BMEN
BMEN 547.title: Immunoengineering

BMEN 548.description: Survey of cardiovascular development, anatomy, physiology and pathology. Recent advances in our understanding of the basic mechanisms of congenital cardiovascular defects and cardiovascular disease. Engineering principles, detection and treatment of cardiovascular defects.
BMEN 548.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 240.
BMEN 548.subject: BMEN
BMEN 548.title: Cardiovascular System: From Development to Disease

BMEN 565.description: Mathematical and theoretical analysis of the mechanical properties and functions of soft biological tissues to include arterial vessels.
BMEN 565.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 263.
BMEN 565.subject: BMEN
BMEN 565.title: Advanced Biomechanics

BMEN 572.description: Molecular basis of bioregenerative engineering; biomaterial design; biocompatibility assessment; cell isolation and characterization; rapid prototyping, scaffold fabrication, and biofabrication; protein and gene delivery; bioreactor design; transport in biological tissues; applications of tissue engineering in regenerative medicine.
BMEN 572.subject: BMEN
BMEN 572.title: Tissue Engineering

BMEN 575.description: Introductory overview of fundamental concepts in science and engineering of soft materials; the relation between microstructure and macroscopic behavior in a variety of soft matter systems; key applications in chemical and biomedical engineering.
BMEN 575.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 122 or MATH 141.
BMEN 575.subject: BMEN
BMEN 575.title: Engineering of Soft Materials

BMEN 589.description: Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title. May be repeated as topic varies.
BMEN 589.subject: BMEN
BMEN 589.title: Special Topics in Biomedical Engineering

BMEN 710.description: Analytical and quantitative techniques applied to engineering problems in biomedical transport, tissue mechanics, celluar and organ physiology, and control of medical devices.
BMEN 710.subject: BMEN
BMEN 710.title: Modeling and Simulation of Biomedical System

BMEN 713.description: Advanced examination of the organization and function of the cell with emphasis on the biophysical and quantitative aspects of cellular function. Emphasis will be on the biomedical engineering applications of regulation of cell division, protein transcription and translation within the cell, cellular energetics, and intracellular networks for cell signaling and cell function.
BMEN 713.subject: BMEN
BMEN 713.title: Human Cell and Molecular Biology for Biomedical Engineers

BMEN 720.description: Conservation of momentum, energy, mass, physico-chemical properties of biofluids, blood rheology, circulation models and cardiovascular regulation, solute and oxygen transport in tissues, gas transport in lungs and respiratory gas exchange models, kinetics and compartmental modeling, modeling of artificial organs.
BMEN 720.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BMEN 354.
BMEN 720.subject: BMEN
BMEN 720.title: Transport Phenomena in Biomedical Systems

BMEN 723.description: An examination of human biological structure and function from an engineering perspective. Engineering principles will be used to analyze anatomical structures and physiological functions at the tissue, organ, and systems levels.
BMEN 723.subject: BMEN
BMEN 723.title: Anatomy and Physiology for Biomedical Engineers

BMEN 795.description: Critical reading and literacy in the biomedical engineering discipline as it relates to students’ research. Graduate Standing in the Biomedical Engineering Program.
BMEN 795.subject: BMEN
BMEN 795.title: Biomedical Engineering Literature

BMEN 797.description: Individual research to be arranged with the instructor. Graduate Standing in the Biomedical Engineering Program.
BMEN 797.subject: BMEN
BMEN 797.title: Biomedical Engineering Doctoral Research

BMEN 798.description: Graduate seminar on current topics in biomedical engineering. Instruction on critical analysis and communication in the discipline.
BMEN 798.subject: BMEN
BMEN 798.title: Graduate Seminar in Biomedical Engineering

BMEN 799.description: Thesis preparation for Masters Program. Graduate Standing in the Biomedical Engineering Program. Grading: Pass/Fail.
BMEN 799.subject: BMEN
BMEN 799.title: Biomedical Engineering Masters Thesis Preparation

BMEN 898.description: Seminar for doctoral students on current biomedical engineering topics and instruction in professional preparation in the discipline. Graduate Standing in the Biomedical Engineering Program.
BMEN 898.subject: BMEN
BMEN 898.title: Doctoral Seminar in Biomedical Engineering

BMEN 899.description: Dissertation preparation for the Ph.D. Program. Graduate standing in the Biomedical Engineering program.
BMEN 899.subject: BMEN
BMEN 899.title: Biomedical Engineering Doctoral Dissertation Preparation
